  "drop_guidance": [
    "Drop bare field labels that name a speaker's industry rather than a transferable idea, unless the talk generalizes from them — 'quantum information science' and 'brain-computer interfaces' should only land on deep tech company building when used as an exemplar of deep-tech company building; otherwise drop.",
    "Drop biographical or single-datapoint anecdotes: 'dropping out of college', 'new business formation data'. These are evidence inside one talk, not concepts other talks can engage, and would produce dead one-talk pages.",
    "Never keep lexical or case variants as separate pages — 'physical ai' / 'physical AI', 'agent harness' / 'harness design' / 'agent harness engineering', 'long-horizon agents' / 'long-horizon agent runs'. Collapse to the canonical name.",
    "Map over-specific one-off techniques up to their parent rather than minting: 'metadata conditioning' and 'human intervention in data collection' → physical ai; 'system prompt ablation' → capability elicitation; 'bitmap typography' → product and visual design craft. Drop only if the parent already fully covers the string and it adds no distinct sense.",
    "Drop strings that merely restate the event's framing or a talk's subject rather than an idea — e.g. 'frontier lab operating model' when it is only describing one lab's org chart (otherwise map to research taste).",
    "Drop generic business-function strings with no AI or startup-stage specificity if no parent claims them; 'performance review design' belongs on founder hiring bar only because it is framed as an early-stage evaluation problem."
  ],
  "notes": "Deliberate separations: (1) 'founder psychology' (resilience, burnout, sustaining yourself) is kept apart from 'contrarian conviction' (non-consensus belief and judgment) — a burnout story is not a conviction story. (2) 'regulatory navigation for startups' (a company routing around or through rules) is kept apart from 'ai policy and regulation' (how the rules themselves get made); a talk by a policymaker goes to the latter, a founder describing FDA/permitting goes to the former. (3) 'ai compute infrastructure' (hardware, energy, physical ceiling) is kept apart from the reused 'inference cost optimization' (per-token unit economics as a product constraint). (4) 'simulation and sim-to-real transfer' was minted rather than reusing AIEWF's 'simulation environments', which is scoped to exercising software agents and simulated users, not physical-system design and embodiment gap. (5) 'iteration speed' spans software, hardware, and design deliberately — it is the cross-domain claim, not a hardware-only concept.\n\nDeliberate merges: 'robot foundation models', 'cross-embodiment transfer', 'end-to-end models', and robot training-data strings all fold into 'physical ai' because this event has too few robotics/AV talks to support separate pages; if assignment finds three or more talks distinctly discussing generalist robot policies, splitting 'robot foundation models' back out is the right call. 'spec-driven development' and 'agentic loop design' exist as exact AIEWF concepts but appear in only one talk each here, so they were folded into 'agentic coding workflows' and 'agent harness design' respectively — cross-event links to those AIEWF pages can still be made from the parent.\n\nAmbiguous boundaries the assignment pass will hit: 'eval and metrics as moat' was placed on 'platform dependency risk' (defensibility against labs) rather than 'evaluation as competitive moat' — if the talk's argument is about measurement practice rather than defensibility, move it. 'agent controllability' sits on 'frontier ai risk' (steerability as a safety property), not on harness design. 'code review as risk management' sits on 'agentic coding workflows' but shades into 'prompt injection defense' when the untrusted input is the agent's own output. 'prompt injection defense' is a thin reuse here (2 aliases, ~2-3 talks) — kept because the cross-event link is worth more than the page density; drop it if assignment finds fewer than three talks."
